The projected lattice sites are precisely -1, 0 and 1. At zero, any combination with endpoints can be grouped into a midpoint between the two endpoint bodies and a convex combination with B. The endpoint midpoint is B/2, strictly contained in B because B is a full-dimensional centered difference body. Under a small endpoint perturbation this inclusion persists by the displayed Minkowski-ball estimate, so the unchanged middle fiber and both endpoint fibers are still actual.

By central symmetry every closed containing cap at the origin has mass at least half the total. The two closed sides of a through-origin plane with nonzero continuous normal each have exactly half the mass, since each fiber trace of the plane is volume-null, and cover every point. Thus this is the actual maximum depth. Every H_{i,a} passes through the origin, cuts complementary endpoint portions under reflection and exactly half of the middle body, and has that same depth mass. The margins in a group sum to zero because its thresholds sum to one. Subtracting different thresholds at a fixed i obtains a pure base direction, and the remaining normals span the continuous dual space.

In original barycentrics the affine vertex matrix preserves the barycentric sum and its determinant is the intrinsic volume multiplier. A fixed proper one-vertex cap has one intercept on each edge from that vertex, giving the product of the fractions. The other fibers contribute constants to cap and total volumes, so each active global budget is equivalent to the original endpoint budget.

At each vertex the eta weights sum to 1/m, with high probability 1/(3m), mean reciprocal threshold m/d and variance 4m^2/[d^2(3m-1)]. The sum of the physical matrix row sums is zero, so the first derivative vanishes. In the second derivative the mean-centered variance contributes -d(d-1) times the variance times 1/m to the column-sum coefficient. The remaining quadratic terms give the stated negative Frobenius term and the coefficient -[m(4d-7)+1]/[d(3m-1)]. The coefficient is negative for every d>=2, and the Frobenius term is strict on any nonzero physical tangent. An independent exact polynomial expansion of the determinant and the cap intercept factors checked the stationary and quadratic terms in dimensions two through four.

The normalized weights for the alternative planar high and low thresholds are 1/30 and 3/20, with per-vertex sum 1/3, mean 3/2 and variance 49/36. The independent expansion gives coefficient -11/27 and the six-dimensional physical tangent has six negative directions. Shoelace gives area three for the hexagon, hence total mass four and depth two. Since the multipliers are positive and the caps are all initially active, feasible volume is bounded above by the stationary Lagrangian with baseline budget constants, so the strict local maximum holds under the imposed fixed endpoint budgets.
